You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC notes: remove isolated noise from a scene of colored blocks

## Solved instance `task-315375b1`

Input 27x24. Background color 9. The coherent object palette is 5, 7, and 8. Output keeps the dimensions and all legitimate shapes, but removes isolated off-scene singleton noise by restoring each noisy cell to the underlying shape color or to background. Do not simply delete all unusual pixels to the background: markers inside shapes must be restored to their object's color.

Two demos established this:
- Demo 1: background 2; coherent shapes include 7 and 1. Singleton noise colors were removed/restored; shape colors and background remain.
- Demo 2: background 3; coherent shapes include 6, 0, 4, and 8. The isolated 7 at row 13, col 2 (0-based) disappears to background; the other large coherent regions (including the 0 blocks) remain. This confirms that color alone is not enough to identify noise: use coherent object geometry / repeated block patterns.

For the solved test, the objects and repairs were:
- 5 blocks: rows 1-2 cols 19-21; rows 8-12 cols 15-16; rows 12-17 cols 4-5; rows 22-25 cols 16-18.
- 7 blocks: rows 8-10 cols 4-9; rows 17-18 cols 13-16; rows 19-24 cols 0-1; rows 23-24 cols 20-21.
- 8 blocks: rows 3-4 cols 4-5; rows 5-11 cols 19-23; rows 14-15 cols 15-21; rows 20-24 cols 8-14.
- Restore corrupted interior cells to their object's color: 7-shape at (8,9) and (10,9); 5-shape at (9,16); 8-shape at (14,21), (20,10), and (24,12); 7-shape at (17,16). Coordinates are zero-based.
- Other isolated speckles outside shapes (mostly 3/4) restore to background 9. Preserve all other cells, including clean block boundaries.

General procedure: infer the background and coherent rectangular/block shapes first. Identify isolated one-cell distractors, then use their position relative to the shapes to restore either the expected shape color (inside a region) or background (outside). Keep the full original grid dimensions. Be careful: an apparent object boundary may be an irregular union of blocks; don't expand an object merely to make a bounding box solid unless the scene evidence supports that repair.

Caution: an earlier draft of these notes had incorrect colors for this test; the description above was checked against the actual task input and accepted output.

## Diagonal ray extension from matching markers (task-db7b98a6; accepted)
When two same-colored cells are adjacent diagonally (one row and one column apart), extend their diagonal line in both directions through background cells, preserving the original grid size and all original cells. Stop a ray at the edge or immediately before any non-background cell (a different colored marker blocks it); do not overwrite obstacles. This is selective: only a diagonal pair initiates an extension. Same-colored orthogonal pairs or isolated singletons do not.

Accepted test: 26x11, background 4. Pair 7 at zero-based (4,7),(5,8) extends NW, adding 7 at (3,6),(2,5),(1,4),(0,3); the SE direction is stopped by existing 8 at (6,9). Pair 6 at (6,8),(7,7) extends down-left, adding 6 at (8,6) through (14,0); its opposite up-right ray is stopped by 8 at (5,9). Preserve the original 8 markers at (5,9),(6,9),(7,10). Accepted after four incorrect submissions.

Demo evidence:
- 23x14, background 1: diagonal 9s at (12,1),(13,2) extended southeast through (22,11) to the boundary; northwest was blocked by 8 at (11,0).
- 10x10, background 4: diagonal 0 pair at (6,9),(7,8) caused no visible changes because the forward ray was immediately blocked by 8 at (8,7), and the opposite ray ran off-grid.
- 27x11, background 9: same-color 6s at (18,7),(19,7) are vertical, not diagonal, so no extension; output unchanged.
- 15x22, background 5: diagonal 2 pair at (10,17),(11,18) extended northwest to top edge at (0,7); southeast was blocked by 9 at (12,19). Other cells preserved.

Procedure: copy the input, identify pairs of equal colors at diagonal offsets (+1,+1) and (+1,-1). For each pair, trace its line beyond both endpoints; fill only background cells with that pair's color, stopping at grid boundary or the first non-background cell. Deduplicate overlaps and preserve all markers. Check immediate blockers; extend both ends only where possible.
